solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Head of Tesco abandons staff cut back

indicators.note: the staff word abandons the Tesco head, so that letter walks out of it

parts.note: a stave is a staff or stick
the head of Tesco is its first letter

explanation.surface: A supermarket boss sacks workers to trim costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' wants to mean employees, as the Tesco surface suggests; here it is a stick, STAVE, and losing its T leaves SAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To save money is to economise, which is what cutting back on spending means.

clue.text: see 23dn.
Flesh out Vince — "not Cameron's main disciple"

indicators.note: 'out' as in out of order: the remaining letters and the disciple are jumbled
'not Cameron's main' tells us to take the leading letter of Cameron away from Vince

parts.note: Vince Cable, the Lib Dem in Cameron's coalition
the main, or leading, letter of Cameron
son in the old sense of a follower or disciple

explanation.surface: Vince Cable is dismissed as no loyal follower of David Cameron in the coalition government.
explanation.walkthrough: VINCE without C is VINE; add SON and rearrange all seven letters to get VENISON. Vince Cable was a Lib Dem minister under Cameron.
explanation.definitionFit: Venison is deer meat, and meat is flesh eaten as food.

clue.text: Aggressive type of idiot TV presenter full of trouble

indicators.note: the idiot and presenter together are full of the trouble, so that word sits between them

parts.note: an ass is a fool
Ant of the British presenting duo Ant and Dec
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A jibe at a foolish TV presenter who has been in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant McPartlin, of Ant and Dec, is half of a hugely popular British TV presenting pair, and he had well-publicised troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is someone who attacks another, so a violent, hostile kind of person.

clue.text: Laid back Ukip leader playing with penis

indicators.note: playing with letters means moving them around, so the leader and the rude word get mixed

parts.note: the leading letter of Ukip
taken as it stands, five letters

explanation.surface: A smutty image of a relaxed Ukip boss, Private Eye style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid back' wants to mean relaxed in manner; it is literal here, lying on one's back. Ukip was the UK Independence Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine describes lying face upward, flat on the back, and also idle or passive.

clue.text: The whole beer plus roll, as so often passes Trump's lips?

definitions.text: as so often passes Trump's lips?

parts.note: the whole is all of it
British slang for beer, as in 'on the piss'
plus is and
to roll up, as yarn or a clock, is to wind

explanation.surface: A lunch order of beer and a bread roll, then a dig at Donald Trump's speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' looks like a bread roll beside the beer; it is the verb, to wind. 'All piss and wind' is British slang for empty bluster.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means boastful talk with no substance, the kind of bluster often attributed to Trump.

clue.text: Reasoned: "Maybe go with CIA to split liberal leaders"

indicators.note: the jumbled letters split the pair of leaders apart by going between them

parts.note: the leading letters of both words, which open and close the answer

indicators.note: 'maybe' says the letters that follow could be arranged another way

parts.note: the anagram fodder, five letters

explanation.surface: A spoof quote proposing that the CIA help divide the Liberal leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: GO and CIA jumble to OGICA, which sits between L and L, the first letters of 'liberal leaders'.
explanation.definitionFit: Logical describes thinking that follows sound steps of argument, which is what reasoned thought does.

clue.text: A screw that eluded Ed Miliband?

definitions.text: A screw that eluded Ed Miliband?

parts.note: the surface reads a screw as a piece of hardware, or a sexual partner who got away
the setter means the prize Miliband failed to win at the 2015 election: the Downing Street home of the Prime Minister

explanation.walkthrough: A screw can be identified by a size number, and Ed Miliband led Labour to defeat in 2015, so the Prime Minister's residence at 10 Downing Street eluded him.
explanation.definitionFit: Number Ten is shorthand for the British Prime Minister's official London residence and office, which Miliband never occupied.

clue.text: A big enticement, blowing up Cameron's lot all in one place?

definitions.text: Cameron's lot all in one place?

indicators.note: blowing something up scatters its parts, so the enticement's letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: the anagram fodder, fourteen letters

explanation.surface: A tempting chance to blow up the whole Cameron government while its ministers sit together.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a terrorist plot; the definition is innocent, just ministers gathered round one table.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameron's lot are his senior ministers, and when they all gather together that assembly is formally held in Downing Street.

clue.text: Ill-begotten gain involving EU pig of sorts

indicators.note: something ill-begotten is badly made, so these letters are formed in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as it stands
taken as it stands

explanation.surface: A complaint about profits made dishonestly from European Union money.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is incomplete by design: a guinea pig is a pig 'of sorts', so GUINEA stands for the first word of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A guinea pig is a rodent rather than a real hog, so the first word names a sort of so-called pig.

clue.text: Simultaneous coupling makes institution very smelly

gamy meat is high and strong-smelling

explanation.surface: Couples getting together at once turns a college rank.
explanation.walkthrough: A poly, short for polytechnic, was a kind of British higher-education college.
explanation.definitionFit: Polygamy is being married to several partners at the same time, so several marriages running concurrently.

clue.text: Luvvie's panties off — front of house captivated

the front letter of house

explanation.surface: An actor strips off and the audience is enthralled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Front of house' is theatre jargon, which suits the surface; here it just gives H. Luvvie is British slang for a gushing actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is an actor, and a luvvie is a jokey British word for an effusive performer.

clue.text: The thing is stifling iconic South American passions

Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary of the famous poster

explanation.walkthrough: 'The thing is' reads as a conversational opener; it is IT'S, which then holds CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Itches are cravings or strong desires, as in an itch to travel, so they are passions.

clue.text: Gender a problem for Tebbit now?

indicators.note: a problem suggests something gone wrong, so these letters are wrongly ordered

parts.note: the anagram fodder, seven letters

explanation.surface: Norman Tebbit, old-school Tory, struggles with modern ideas of gender.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman Tebbit was a hard-line Thatcher minister, now an elderly Conservative peer, so the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a senior, distinguished figure in a party, which describes the retired Conservative veteran well.

clue.text: Political correctness puts end to the Conservative dickhead in rough surroundings?

indicators.note: the parts sit in the rough surroundings, which wrap round them

parts.note: rude means rough or crude, forming the outside
the last letter of 'the'
standard abbreviation
a tit is a fool

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: rectitude is moral correctness, and 'Political' is added for the Private Eye joke about the Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: Rectitude is moral uprightness and proper conduct, a kind of correctness in behaviour.

clue.text: Writer's forsaken prick (oxygen-dead) cut off

the chemical symbol
the late means the dead

explanation.walkthrough: 'Forsaken prick' is colour for a person left alone, which is also what an isolate is.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to separate from others, which is to sever someone from contact.

clue.text: Rogue drug taken by late pop star — that'll teach you

E is ecstasy
a cad is a rogue

explanation.surface: A cautionary tale about drugs and a dead singer: that'll teach you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That'll teach you' reads as a moral; it defines a place of learning. Amy Winehouse struggled with drugs, which fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a school or college, a place whose purpose is instruction of its students.

clue.text: Tosspot Duke skating on thin ice here with Brenda?

parts.note: standard abbreviation
where one skates on ice
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The Duke of Edinburgh, a fool, taking risks alongside the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skating on thin ice' wants to mean taking a risk; read literally it points to the RINK. Brenda is Private Eye's long-running name for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A tosspot is an old word for a heavy boozer, someone who drinks too much.

clue.text: Mo elected with half of comedy act (Tory leader)

parts.note: an elected candidate is in
Stan Laurel of the double act Laurel and Hardy
the first letter of Tory

explanation.definitionFit: A mo is informal British shorthand for a moment, and an instant is a very brief moment.

clue.text: Have a cheeky go at screwing Tory nit

clue.text: see 23dn.
Base, Archer-style, liable to go under?

clue.text: Nothing on, Heather's an ugly little thing, maybe

clue.text: "Rocky agrees to take top off" scandal — don't join!

clue.text: Creep Nick lacks power
